subChunks.title: IS NULL and IS NOT NULL
subChunks.hookHtml: NULL is not a value — it is the absence of one. You cannot test for it with =. You need IS NULL.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Why = NULL never works

-- This always returns zero rows:
SELECT * FROM apprentices WHERE mentor_id = NULL;

-- This works:
SELECT * FROM apprentices WHERE mentor_id IS NULL;

The expression NULL = NULL evaluates to UNKNOWN, not TRUE. SQL uses three-valued logic: TRUE, FALSE, UNKNOWN. WHERE only passes rows where the condition is TRUE — UNKNOWN rows are filtered out just like FALSE rows.

IS NOT NULL

SELECT name FROM apprentices WHERE mentor_id IS NOT NULL;

NULL in arithmetic and functions

Any arithmetic involving NULL produces NULL: xp + NULL = NULL. Most aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG) ignore NULL values silently — knowing this prevents silent wrong totals.

COALESCE — provide a fallback

SELECT name, COALESCE(mentor_id, 0) AS mentor
FROM apprentices;

COALESCE(a, b) returns a if it is not NULL, otherwise b. It is the standard way to substitute a default for a NULL.

storyBeats.text: Cipher points to a column in the ledger where some cells are simply blank — not zero, not empty, just absent.

storyBeats.speaker: Cipher the Archivist
storyBeats.text: NULL is not zero. It is not empty. It is the absence of information. Comparing with = NULL always gives UNKNOWN — and UNKNOWN rows vanish from your results. Always use IS NULL or IS NOT NULL to test for absence.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain why `WHERE col = NULL` always returns zero rows in SQL, and what you should write instead.

questions.prompt: Why does `WHERE col = NULL` always return zero rows?
options: NULL = NULL evaluates to UNKNOWN, not TRUE, so no rows pass the WHERE filter
NULL is treated as zero and zero does not equal NULL
SQL does not allow = in NULL comparisons
The column must be declared NOT NULL for = to work
questions.answer: NULL = NULL evaluates to UNKNOWN, not TRUE, so no rows pass the WHERE filter
questions.explanation: SQL uses three-valued logic: TRUE, FALSE, UNKNOWN. Any comparison involving NULL produces UNKNOWN. WHERE only passes TRUE rows — UNKNOWN is filtered out just like FALSE.

questions.prompt: Which clause correctly finds rows where `score` is missing?
questions.explanation: IS NULL is the correct SQL operator for testing the absence of a value. = NULL, == NULL, and IS EMPTY are not valid SQL for this purpose.

questions.prompt: What does `SELECT COALESCE(mentor_id, -1) FROM apprentices WHERE id = 4` return when mentor_id is NULL?
questions.explanation: COALESCE returns the first non-NULL argument. Since mentor_id is NULL, it falls through to -1.

questions.prompt: A table has 100 rows. 10 rows have NULL in column `score`. What does `SELECT AVG(score) FROM t` return?
options: The average of the 90 non-NULL values — NULLs are ignored by AVG
The average of all 100 rows, treating NULL as 0
questions.answer: The average of the 90 non-NULL values — NULLs are ignored by AVG
questions.explanation: Standard aggregate functions (SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, COUNT(col)) silently ignore NULL values. COUNT(*) counts all rows; COUNT(score) counts only non-NULL score values.
